# Questions for the client

The return above is complete on stated assumptions; these answers would confirm or change specific figures. Each question names the number it moves.

1. **Household size on Form 8962.** Does Leo live with you more than half the year, and is he included in your household even though you are not claiming him for 2025? The 1095-A lists four covered individuals and the library's poverty line is the **family-of-4** figure ($31,200), which is what I used (292.79% FPL). If the correct household is 3 people, my figures for the applicable figure (5.7115%), the credit ($7,531.26) and the repayment ($1,900) all change — and I cannot compute a family-of-3 version because that poverty line is not in the library.

2. **Leo's 2025 dependency.** Please confirm the father is claiming Leo on his 2025 return and that you signed/delivered the Form 8332 release for 2025 (the decree requires it in odd years). If he is *not* claiming Leo, tell me — that is worth $2,200 of child tax credit and would change the refund from $2,322 to about $4,522. Also confirm Sofia lived with you more than half the year.

3. **The Brooklyn lease (this is the biggest single risk).** Please send the current lease and the rent history for 318 Dean St #4B. I allowed the full rental loss because the library treats a never-raised, below-market rent charged to an **unrelated long-term tenant** as not triggering the personal-use rule "if the rent is a fair rental for that lease" — but the lease is only referenced in the prior-year file, so the position rests on your summary. If the rent is held **not** to be a fair rental for that lease (for example a side arrangement, free parking, or a family relationship), the entire $21,018 loss is disallowed. That would push AGI to $110,900 and taxable income to $79,400, which is **outside the tax table in my library**, so I could not even finish the federal tax figure.

4. **New York residency end date.** I used **June 30, 2025** (Brooklyn lease ended, you were "out by then") = 181 resident days, 184 nonresident days. Do you agree, or should the change date be July 3 (Tampa closing)? Also: did either of you keep a NY dwelling available, a NY driver's license, NY voter registration, or NY homestead/domicile indicia after June 30?

5. **Health coverage period.** The 1095-A shows January–June marketplace coverage for all four of you, and Elena's W-2 shows employer coverage (code DD) July–December. Please confirm there was **no** marketplace coverage after June and that no second 1095-A (or a second policy/period) exists. I also want confirmation that the stray "21–26" line on the form is a printing artifact and not additional covered months — 12 months of advance payments instead of 6 would roughly double the excess advance credit.

6. **Why is each of you working remotely from Florida?** For Marcus: does Reyes & Pike Consulting Inc require him to be at the NYC office, or is remote entirely his own preference? For Elena: is Halvorsen's "fully remote" arrangement a business requirement (e.g. no NY workspace available, a client site in Florida, a written remote-work agreement) or an accommodation she requested? This is decisive for New York: unless the out-of-state work is for the **employer's necessity**, the convenience rule makes **all** $122,000 of wages NY source for the whole year (instead of about $60,500 on a 181/365 day count). Any written remote-work policy or letter would help.

7. **Missing items that would change federal numbers.** Please send: any 1099s or brokerage statements (dividends, capital gains, a 1099-DIV/k-1 for anything else), 2025 estimated tax payments or prior-year overpayment applied to 2025, IRA/HSA contributions, child or dependent care expenses (Form 2441), any 2025 student loan interest, any 2025 real property tax bills for the Tampa home and any personal property tax (city/county), and the condo's prior-year depreciation schedule and purchase/allocation documentation.

8. **New York return scope.** The NY tax due and the refund of $6,752 of NY withholding cannot be computed from my library (no NY rate schedule or deductions). Do you want the full IT-203 prepared from NY materials you provide, and did you also have any NY nonresident-period items I have not seen (NY bank interest, NY lottery/gambling winnings, a NY part-year NY rental other than the condo)?

9. **S-corp basis plan.** $16,500 of Marcus's loss is suspended and unusable until he restores basis. Do you intend to contribute cash or make a **direct loan** to Reyes & Pike (a guarantee of the bank line does not count)? Tell me about any planned 2026 contributions before you sign anything — it changes the value of the carryforward.

10. **Marcus's S-corp compensation.** Is the $68,000 W-2 wage from the S-corp reasonable relative to his services, and was there any other S-corp distribution in 2025? (Distributions of $12,000 in 2023 and $5,200 in 2024 were within basis, so no gain — but if there were additional 2025 distributions the basis computation changes.)
